LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a straightforward build script for the R package `r-tidyplots`, an open-source library for creating tidy scientific plots. The `source` line fetches exclusively from the official CRAN repository (https://cran.r-project.org), and both md5sums and b2sums are provided to verify the tarball integrity. There are no suspicious network requests, no downloads from unrelated hosts, and no use of dangerous commands like `curl|bash`, `eval`, or base64-decoding of fetched content.

The `build()` function uses `R CMD INSTALL -l build`, which installs the package into a local `build/` directory rather than directly into `$pkgdir` — this is an unconventional build approach, but it is legitimate: the `package()` function then copies the built package from `build/` into `$pkgdir/usr/lib/R/library` and installs the upstream LICENSE file into the standard licenses path. All file operations remain scoped to the package directory (`$pkgdir`), the local build directory, or files within the fetched tarball itself; nothing touches unrelated system paths, user home directories, or exfiltrates data.

The only minor observation is the maintainer field listing "AutoUpdateBot" with an arch4edu.org email, suggesting automated maintenance, but this does not indicate malicious intent — the script content itself is clean, readable, and consistent with standard R packaging practices. No evidence of injected payload, backdoor, or supply-chain compromise was found.
</details>

</summary>
</security_assessment>
